title: Video Production Manager (Remote)
description: Video Production Manager (Remote) Experienced Video Production Manager Required We are looking for a highly experienced Video Production Manager to join our team and take ownership of video production across a range of exciting projects. This is not an entry-level editing role. We are looking for somebody who has spent years producing high-quality video content and understands the complete production process from raw footage through to final delivery. You should be comfortable editing content yourself while also managing production workflows, quality control, and creative execution. This role would suit someone who takes genuine pride in their work and who notices the small details that others miss. --- About Us We are a growing marketing and technology company that supports professional service businesses. We produce a wide range of content including podcasts, webinars, educational content, social media videos, interviews, thought leadership content, and promotional materials. Our clients expect work that is professional, polished, and delivered to a consistently high standard. Quality matters enormously to us. We are not looking for somebody who can simply assemble clips together. We are looking for somebody who understands storytelling, audience engagement, brand consistency, and professional production standards. If you're the type of person who notices the details others miss and takes pride in delivering exceptional work, we'd love to hear from you. --- What You'll Be Doing You will be responsible for producing and managing a variety of video content including: - Long-form podcast episodes - Webinar recordings - YouTube videos - Social media content - Short-form video clips and reels - Client case studies - Educational content - Event footage - Promotional videos - Internal training materials You will: - Edit videos to a professional standard - Create engaging short-form clips from long-form content - Add graphics, captions, transitions, and motion elements where appropriate - Improve audio quality and visual presentation - Ensure all content meets brand standards - Perform final quality assurance before publication - Organise video assets and project files - Coordinate with designers, writers, project managers, and other tea ---------- mbers - Continuously improve production workflows using the latest tools and technologies --- Software & Tools You should already be highly proficient in one or more of the following: - Adobe Premiere Pro - Adobe After Effects - Adobe Audition - DaVinci Resolve - CapCut - Opus Clip - Descript - Riverside - Canva - Other modern AI-assisted video production tools We are not concerned with which tools you use. We care about the quality of the final result. You should actively stay up to date with emerging AI and video production technologies that improve speed without sacrificing quality. --- Essential Requirements Experience - Minimum 10 years of professional experience in video production, editing, or post-production - Proven portfolio of professional work - Experience producing content for business audiences - Experience working remotely with distributed teams - Strong understanding of video storytelling, pacing, audience retention, and content repurposing English You must have excellent English skills. Particular attention will be paid to: - Written English - Caption accuracy - Grammar - Punctuation - Professional communication All work must be delivered in UK English. Attention to Detail This is absolutely critical. We operate a formal quality assurance process and maintain exceptionally high standards across all content we produce. You should naturally notice: - Spelling mistakes - Caption errors - Audio problems - Timing issues - Branding inconsistencies - Incorrect formatting - Visual distractions - Technical mistakes If people regularly tell you that you have a great eye for detail or that you always spot things others miss, then you may be exactly who we are looking for. --- Personal Attributes We are looking for someone who is: - Highly organised - Reliable and dependable - Proactive rather than reactive - Calm under pressure - Able to manage multiple projects simultaneously - Committed to continuous improvement - Comfortable receiving feedback - Passionate about producing exceptional work Most importantly, we want somebody who genuinely cares about quality and takes ownership of their work. --- Working With Our Team Our team works remotely and collaborates daily using: - Slack - Google Meet - Google Workspace - Project Management Software You should be comfortable communicating regularly with colleagues and participating in project discussions when required. When working with us, you are expected to be available and responsive during agreed working hours. --- Training Full training will be provided regarding our internal processes, quality standards, and workflows. However, this is not a role for somebody who is still learning video production. You should be capable of hitting the ground running from day one. --- How To Apply Please apply online by sending in your details using our recruitment website: ---------- Please include: - Your CV - Portfolio - Examples of long-form content - Examples of short-form content - Details of the software and tools you regularly use - A short introduction explaining why you believe you would be a good fit for this role --- Please Note: References We always take references before onboarding any new tea ---------- mber. You must be able to provide up to three professional references. No exceptions will be made. Thank you for your understanding. --- We look forward to hearing from you.

RESPONSIBILITIES • Organize and manage large collections of travel photos and videos • Create logical folder structures and archival systems • Select and organize the strongest images for storytelling purposes • Create traveler photo packages • Assist with memory books and tabletop photo books • Create reels, short videos, and highlight videos • Create social media content from travel experiences • Help tell the story of destinations, travelers, events, and experiences • Create content that balances: Traveler memories Historical sites Local culture Architecture Food experiences Behind-the-scenes ---------- nts Fun travel memories • Build organized content libraries for future marketing and promotional use • Help develop simple ways for older travelers to access and enjoy their travel memories REQUIRED SKILLS • Canva • Video Editing • Social Media Content Creation • Strong Organizational Skills • Excellent English Communication BONUS SKILLS • Travel Industry Experience • Photography • Photoshop • CapCut • Scrapbooking or Memory Book Design • Google Photos • >Facebook Com munities • Shopify • Trello • AI Tools such as ChatGPT TO APPLY Put "Photo Crown" in your subject line. Submit your resume. Submit a 2-3 minute video introduction. Submit your desired hourly rate. Submit a portfolio with MULTIPLE examples of your work. IMPORTANT Applicants who do NOT provide a portfolio with multiple examples of their work will NOT be considered. We are especially interested in seeing: • Travel Videos • Event Videos • Reels • Storytelling Projects • Memory Books • Photo Organization Projects • Before-and-After Editing Examples • Projects involving people, experiences, and events Product-only portfolios are not a strong fit for this position. FINAL QUESTION Imagine you have been given 500 photos and 50 videos from our Ohio Salute to Veterans event. Please tell us: • How would you organize the photos and videos? • What final products would you create for the attendees? • What content would you create for Facebook , YouTube, Instagram, and Google Business? • How would you make it easy for women aged 60-90 to access and enjoy their memories? • What would be your first three steps if we hired you for this project? description: Overview I am looking for a skilled video editor to edit 2 short-form direct response video ads for my marketing company. One video is for  targeting employment lawyers and one is for Medicare insurance agents. Both videos are already shot — raw footage is ready. I will leave you with the google rive to open and view video to see how you can do it. These are paid ad videos that will run on Facebook and Instagram. They need to be punchy, fast, professional, and built to stop the scroll and convert viewers into leads. Reference Style The editing style I want is inspired by the Instagram ---------- (Reaz & Harley). Go look at their page before applying. Key elements I want: ---------- Walking and talking format with gimbal movement Fast cuts between locations and angles Whip pan transitions between scenes Animated text overlays that appear in sync with spoken words — bold, clean, not overdone. Keep text minimal and impactful, not every single word on screen PROFFESSIONAL - i want mine more professional and clean Music underneath that matches the pace and tone — motivational, modern, not distracting Subtle sound effects on text appearances and transitions The overall feel should be confident, peer-to-peer, and direct. Not hype. Not flashy. Just sharp and credible. Video 1 — Employment Lawyers Approximate Length: 75 seconds Script / What Was Said On Camera: "Most plaintiff employment lawyers I talk to are doing fine on referrals and word-of-mouth. Here's what they don't realize — 97% of employment cases never reach a lawyer. Because the people with the cases don't even know they have one. They just got fired. They're scared about rent. They're scrolling Instagram — they're not Googling 'employment lawyer near me.' That's where we find them. Before your competitors even know they exist. You don't need someone teaching you employment law. You need to stop missing the cases your competitors aren't even hunting for. Here's how we work. One — exclusive employment cases delivered to your firm every month. Wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, FMLA, retaliation, class actions, unpaid wages. Two — every lead is screened against statute of limitations, residency, attorney status, and case fit. About seventy-five percent get disqualified before your team ever sees them. Three — zero upfront cost. No setup. No retainer. We fund the ad budget. You only pay when your firm signs a case. We've run Meta ads for plaintiff firms since 2019. Thousands of signed cases. If we don't deliver, you don't pay. Three spots open this quarter. Apply at the link below." Text Overlays to Burn In (these must appear on screen at the right ---------- nt): I will provide 1-2 screenshots showing real case results or ad performance. Place these at the authority section — right when the speaker says "We've run Meta ads for plaintiff firms since 2019. Thousands of signed cases." Show the image on screen for 2-3 seconds with a subtle zoom or slide-in animation. Do not just cut hard to it — make it feel natural and credible. Pacing Notes: Video 2 — Medicare Insurance Agents do not cut content, let it breathe naturally) Script / What Was Said On Camera: "Medicare agents — if you've built your Medicare book through grassroots, we'll fill your next webinar with fifteen to twenty-five qualified T65 leads showing up live, or we'll cover the cost of your next webinar campaign. This is specifically for the agent who's already done the work. They've worked T65 lists, sat at kitchen tables, leaned on referrals, and written their first fifty or one hundred policies the hard way — one conversation at a time. You don't need lead training. What you need is a predictable system that puts qualified T65 prospects on your screen every week, so you can stop grinding for every single appointment. If that's you, here's what we deliver. Number one — fifteen to twenty-five qualified T65 leads showing up live to every webinar you run. Locally targeted, age-qualified, voluntarily registered to learn about Medicare. Number three — cost per acquired customer seventy to eighty-five percent lower than direct mail. Roughly two hundred dollars CAC versus twelve hundred plus with direct mail. You can run a webinar every week in your territory without burning your renewals on marketing spend. And we guarantee it. Fifteen to twenty-five qualified T65 attendees on every webinar, or we pay for your next campaign. The only reason we can offer that is because after generating thousands of leads across Medicare agents nationwide, we know exactly what works. along with running them for our agency. One important note — this is NOT for brand-new agents looking for their first ten clients. You need experiewnce, real product knowledge, and the confidence to teach a room of people on a screen. If that's not you, this is not the right system for you yet. This system rewards agents who know they can convert — they just need to meet more qualified seniors at scale. If that is you, click the link below, complete the brief application, and book your webinar gameplan call. We'll show you exactly how this scales in your specific territory. And remember — we guarantee fifteen to twenty-five attendees, or you get a free webinar campaign. So there is no risk in seeing if this will work for you. Click the link below. title: Social Media Video Editor
description: We are looking for a fast, creative, and self-directed social media video editor to join our team as a full-time, long-term contractor. This role moves quickly, the volume is high, and the work is the kind you can actually be proud to put your name on. **What you will be doing:** We operate a booth at live events, like State Fairs, where multiple people are filmed performing shoe cleaning and restoration. Your job is to take that raw daily footage and cut individual clips for each person, each with their own personality, styling, and presence. Every person who sits in that chair has a unique story and your edits need to reflect that. At the same time, all content must align with our brand guidelines. You will be balancing individual personality with brand consistency across every piece you deliver, every day. This is not a slow creative process. Footage comes in, it gets edited, it goes out. The expectation is a high volume of finished, ready-to-post clips on a daily turnaround. You will have the creative latitude to make great content but you will not have someone looking over your shoulder on every edit. You need to be able to own your work and deliver without constant direction. **What we need from you technically:** - You are fast and fluent in your editing software. Premiere Pro, CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, whatever your tool is, you know it well enough that the software is never the bottleneck. - You understand how to cut for social media. Short form, vertical format, pacing, captions, audio sync. You know what performs and you edit with that in mind. - You can work within a set of brand guidelines and apply them consistently across a high volume of content without needing to be reminded. - Your portfolio shows variety. We want to see that you can make something feel personal to one individual and then shift tone completely for the next. **Communication matters as much as the output:** This role has minimal oversight by design, which means you need to be someone we can trust and talk to. If something is unclear, if footage is missing, or if you have a creative question, you need to be comfortable picking up a call or jumping into a live meeting and working through it directly. Strong verbal communication in English is required. We need to be able to have a real conversation with you. **What this looks like for you:** - Full-time contractor, 40 hours per week - Remote - High volume, fast-paced work with real creative ownership - Stable, ongoing role with a growing pipeline of events and content - 13th month bonus **To apply:** Send us your portfolio or reel. We want to see short-form social media content, ideally event or lifestyle work. Tell us what software you use, how you handle high-volume turnarounds, and what your editing process looks like when you are working fast. We interview for communication and fit as much as we do for skill.

description: Starts part-time. You can stay part-time permanently, or shift to full-time within the first 30 days if you're a good match. Your choice. Now read this whole thing before you apply. It matters. If you're looking for full-time work and you've been struggling to find the right fit, this could be a big deal for you. For the first 30 days, this will definitely be part-time. But if you turn out to be a good match and you want full-time, you could shift over to full-time as early as that first month, or right after it. And if part-time is exactly what you want, you can stay part-time permanently. We're flexible on the hours. The one thing we're not flexible on is that we're looking for someone permanent. If you've ever felt frustrated being treated like just another applicant in a stack of hundreds, this will feel different too. I read every complete application myself, and I'm looking for one or two people I can grow with for years. Here's something most job posts won't tell you. I care more about your mindset than your skill. The person I want shows up with good energy, works well with others, takes instruction openly, and actually wants to learn. Skills I can teach. Mindset I can't. If you bring positive energy and you're happy to do the work, you'll do well here. If you're looking for a place to coast or complain, please apply somewhere else. About the work This is mostly short-form video editing, with some long-form too. Mainly talking-head videos. Our main tools are CapCut and Submagic, and you'll use them every day. You'll also post finished videos to social platforms like TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Facebook , and LinkedIn. We use our own posting platform and our own method for getting video out at scale, so part of the job is learning our specific way of doing things. None of it has a steep learning curve. If you can use CapCut, you can do the editing. The rest is teachable. You'll work directly with me, but you won't be working alone. We're a team. We have daily meetings, and once you're in, you become part of that team. So you'll have people around you, not just a pile of assignments dropped in your lap. Extra skills help, so tell me about them CapCut and Submagic are our main tools. But if you've got skills in Premiere or Photoshop, that's a real plus. Not essential, but it helps. And if you've got any other technical skills at all, I want to hear about them. Don't be shy. The more you can do, the more valuable you are to me. The money, and how it grows I'm not going to hide the numbers from you. This starts part-time, 20 hours a week. To start: $350 per month After your 30-day trial: $400 per month After two more months: $500 per month After that: regular reviews with raises based on how you develop and the value you bring You won't get a raise every single month. The first few bumps are just to get you up to pay that motivates you. Then it settles into regular reviews. Pay comes every two weeks, in USD, on time, every time. No waiting a full month, no chasing payments. One more thing, and read this carefully Here's what I learned the hard way. The single biggest difference between someone who works out and someone who doesn't is English. Not "fluent on paper." Actually being able to talk back and forth with me, clearly, both ways. If I can't communicate with you and you can't communicate with me, neither of us can do this job. So I need to hear you, not just read you. To apply, do these two things. If you skip either one, I'll delete your application without reading it. Put "peanut butter" in the subject line. This tells me you read the whole post. Send me a one-minute Loom video. Talk about anything you want, but tell me a little about your background and your experience. One minute is plenty. I just need to hear you talk. That's it. No agencies. I'm only hiring individuals, not companies. I'm hiring two people to start, both on a 30-day trial. At the end of the trial, I'll keep both, keep one, or part ways with both. So show me who you are.

Three pillars to this role: 1. Editing. You can cut a UGC ad in your sleep — hooks, pacing, captions, sound design, the works. 2. Sourcing B-roll. Half the battle is taste — knowing the exact shot that lands the message — and the other half is research speed. 3. Generating B-roll and A-roll with AI. If we need a shot of a woman pouring coffee at 6am with golden hour lighting and the sourced clips look generic, you should be able to generate that in Higgsfield or Flow inside an hour and have it cut into the edit by end of day. The editors who win in 2026 are the ones who can move fluidly between all three: cut creator UGC, source perfect supporting clips, and generate the impossible shots. That's what we're hiring for. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING - Editing 5–15 ad variants per week across multiple brands - Cutting hooks (we usually test 3–5 hook variants per concept, same body) - Pacing edits for direct response — fast cuts, motion, pattern interrupts, captioned throughout - title: AI Video Creator Flow + Veo 3.1 + CapCut (Full-Time)
job_title: AI Video Creator Flow + Veo 3.1 + CapCut (Full-Time)
description: What You Will Be Doing You will be producing 10-15 short-form videos per day (25-120 seconds each) for health and wellness pages on Instagram and Facebook . Every morning, you receive a Google Drive folder for each reel — it includes a full production file (every image prompt, video prompt, and dialogue line already written) plus all the reference images you need. Your job is to follow it and turn it into a polished, ready-to-post vertical reel using AI tools and CapCut Pro. This is a production role — 95% of it is execution. You do not write scripts. You do not make creative decisions about content. The only creative judgment you make is ensuring visual continuity from scene to scene — backgrounds, props, wardrobe, and prop placement should flow naturally as the video progresses. If a clip breaks continuity (wrong background, prop disappears, character looks different), you regenerate or adjust. Spotting these is the single most important skill — the difference between a video that gets 10k views and one that gets 100k. The Video Style You Will Produce Full Avatar + B-Roll Cuts. The AI character takes up most of the screen and speaks directly to camera. The video cuts to AI-generated b-roll ---------- nts at key points in the script. Captions and overlays appear throughout. This is the style used for personal, authority-building wellness content. Each production file tells you exactly which scenes need character vs b-roll, and includes the exact image prompts and video prompts for each scene. Tools You Need To Have (required to apply) - Google AI Pro OR Google AI Ultra subscription - CapCut Pro subscription Tools I Provide (after signing) - ElevenLabs — Generate AI voice for select reels using the cloned voice I provide (used on roughly 1 in 4 reels — the rest use the voice built into Veo 3.1) - Veo 3.1 — Turn images into ~8 second video clips with voice - Google Gemini Ultra account — Flow image generation + higher rate limits - Nano Banana Pro — High-quality reference images - Google Drive — Receive production folders, deliver finished videos I will train you on the exact workflow for each tool. Previous experience is a plus but not required — what matters is your ability to learn fast and follow detailed instructions. Basic Editing Skills Needed - Stitching multiple 8-second Veo clips into one coherent video - Spotting visual continuity breaks and fixing them - Adding accurate captions - Cutting dead space, tightening pacing - Minor effects: dynamic zoom, transitions, overlays - Attention to timing and pacing — small details separate viral content from average content Requirements - Active Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription (required) - Active CapCut Pro subscription (required) - Strong CapCut / video editing skills (you must demonstrate this in the recreate assignments below) - Excellent English reading comprehension — production files are detailed and must be followed precisely - Extremely detail-oriented - Reliable, fast internet connection - Available 6-8 hours per day, 5-6 days per week (consistency matters more than fixed hours) - PH timezone or similar - Can receive payments via PayPal - Comfortable learning AI tools (I will train you, but you must be a fast and eager learner) - Good at taking direct feedback and improving fast Pay - Starting: $400/month - Performance raise: $500+/month once you are consistently producing high-quality videos at speed - Big bonuses when content performs well ($50 per 1 million views) - Payment via PayPal, monthly - This is a long-term position. I am building a content network and need someone who can grow with it. The Bigger Picture This is my first VA hire. I am building a content network across multiple wellness brands and I need someone who can grow with me, not just clock hours. The right person here has a clear path to: - $1,000+/month earnings as output and quality scale - A manager role training the next VAs I hire — once you have the workflow locked, you teach it - Real input into how my team operates, what we systemize, what we build next If you want a paycheck only, this is not the role for you. If you want to plant a flag and grow with an operator who is moving fast, this is rare and I will know it when I see it. How to Apply — Two-Stage Recreate Process + Interview Call To apply, you must complete a two-stage recreate process so I can evaluate your skills. This replaces a traditional interview — your work speaks for itself. You will use your own Google AI Pro/Ultra account and your own CapCut Pro throughout. Stage 1 — Recreate 1: Exact Reproduction I will send you: - A reel from my own account - The single reference image I used to make it Your task: Recreate the video as exactly as you can. Match the Nano Banana Pro image generations, the cuts, the editing, and the voice. I want to see your best attempt at reverse-engineering my style. You have 24 hours from receiving the materials to submit via Google Drive: - The finished video (mp4) - A Google Doc with every prompt you wrote — the image prompts AND the Veo prompts. I want to see your thinking, not just the output. - 2-3 sentences on your process: what you noticed about the original, what was hard, what you'd improve. This tests your ability to study a video, reverse-engineer it, and write the prompts that produce something close. This is the most important part of the application. I will review and respond within 24-48 hours. Stage 2 — Recreate 2: Independent Production (only if Recreate 1 is approved) If your Recreate 1 looks strong, I will approve you to move on and send you a production file with all prompts already written. Your task: Produce the complete video from the file. No tutorial, no walkthrough — just execute. You have 24 hours from receiving the materials to submit via Google Drive: - The finished video (mp4) This tests your ability to read a production file and turn it into a polished reel — which is exactly what you will do every day in this role. Stage 3 — The Call If both recreates look strong, we hop on a 15 to 30-minute video call. I will walk you through my full workflow live — exactly how I produce these videos — so you understand what you are signing up for. You will have time to ask me anything and tell me why you would be a great fit. This is how I make the final decision. To Apply, Send a Message With: - Confirmation that you have an active Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription AND an active CapCut Pro subscription - Your CapCut / video editing experience (specific examples, portfolio links, or a brief description of what you have edited before) - Any experience with AI tools (Veo, Google Flow, Nano Banana, ElevenLabs, HeyGen, Kling, etc.) — even minimal - Your availability (hours per day, days per week, timezone) - One paragraph on why you would be a great fit for this role - Confirming you will deliver Recreate 1 within 24 hours of receiving the materials, and Recreate 2 within 24 hours of approval to move on I will respond within 12 hours of your application with the Recreate 1 materials. This is a production role, not a creative role. If you thrive on following clear systems, delivering consistent quality, and getting better every day, this is for you.

Advanced Figma proficiency including: Auto Layout Components Variants Variables/Tokens Prototyping Proven experience creating, maintaining, documenting, and scaling design systems. Ability to explain design decisions clearly and justify usability choices with structured reasoning. Ability to independently move projects from ambiguity to execution. Strong understanding of UX principles and interaction design, not just visual execution. Ability to simplify complex workflows into intuitive experiences. Strong systems thinking and attention to detail. Ability to create clear developer handoff documentation and specifications. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ideal Experience Experience in crypto, fintech, investing, payments, or trading products. Understanding of user onboarding, KYC flows, compliance-driven experiences, and financial products. Familiarity with product analytics, user testing, conversion optimization, and experimentation. Basic understanding of front-end development, responsive design, and technical constraints. Experience working in startup environments with fast iteration cycles. Familiarity with modern AI-assisted workflows and tools such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Lovable, v0, or similar. This role is for you if: You think like a product builder, not just a designer. You can clearly explain the reasoning behind your design decisions. You proactively identify problems and propose solutions before being asked. You communicate effectively and collaborate well with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You are comfortable owning projects without constant direction or management. You care about outcomes, not just deliverables. You challenge category norms and bring fresh thinking to product experiences. You can make complex functionality feel obvious within seconds. Nice to Have: Crypto trading experience. Fintech or investment product experience. Motion design experience. Experience conducting user interviews and usability testing. Familiarity with front-end frameworks and developer workflows. Compensation: Starting at $700+/month, depending on experience and fit. Bi-weekly payments via Wise, or direct to bank account method. These are your daily tools, not occasional ones. - **Typography & layout** — You have strong opinions about type hierarchy, spacing, and readability at small scales (packaging, labels, inserts). ### Strong Plus - **Motion graphics** — After Effects or similar for social content, product animations - **3D mockups** — Blender, Dimension, or similar for product visualization - **AI image tools** — Midjourney, DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, or similar for concepting and asset generation - **Figma** — For collaborative design, UI work, or rapid prototyping - **Medical/health product design** — Experience with FDA-regulated labels (Drug Facts panels, mandatory copy) - **Bilingual English** — Your English needs to be strong enough to read briefs, present concepts, and explain design decisions in writing --- ## Screening Questions (Answer All 4) > **Include the phrase "I design for production" somewhere in your application.** This tells us you read the full listing. ### Q1: Packaging Portfolio Piece Show us one packaging project you're most proud of — something that went to physical production. Tell us: - What was the product? - What were the print specs and constraints? - What was your process from concept to final production file? - Show the final printed result (photo of the physical product) alongside your design file if possible. ### Q2: Amazon Listing Challenge Pick one of these two scenarios and walk us through how you'd approach it: **Option A:** Our first aid kit's main image has a 3% click-through rate (below category average of 4.5%). The current image is a straight product shot on white. What would you change and why? What would you A/B test first? **Option B:** We need to create 7 listing images for a new luggage product. Walk us through what each image slot would contain and why, based on what you know converts on Amazon. ### Q3: Two Brands, One Designer SurviveX is medical/tactical (red, black, authoritative). Aerotrunk is travel/lifestyle (modern, aspirational, premium). How do you switch between two very different brand identities without the work starting to look the same? Give us a specific technique or process you use. ### Q4: Tools & Speed What's your full design stack? For each major tool, tell us honestly: daily driver, weekly, or occasional? Also: what's your typical turnaround for a set of 7 Amazon listing images from brief to final delivery? --- ## Paid Test Task Instead of multiple interview rounds, we'll ask our shortlisted candidates to complete a **paid design test** ($75 USD). This lets us evaluate real work, not interview performance. The test will involve: - Redesigning one existing Amazon listing image set (3 images) for SurviveX - Creating one packaging insert concept (front/back) based on a provided dieline and brief You'll receive brand guidelines, existing assets, and a clear brief. We're looking for design quality, brand interpretation, production-readiness, and turnaround speed. --- ## What You Get - **$2,000 USD/month** — paid biweekly, direct deposit - **13th month pay** — standard Philippine labor benefit - **Paid time off** — Philippine holidays + 15 days personal leave - **Creative ownership** — You're not a pixel-pusher. You'll influence brand direction. - **Small team** — Direct access to founders. No layers of middle management. Your ideas get heard. - **Growth** — As the brands grow, you grow. This could become a design lead / creative director path. --- ## How to Apply 1. Answer all 4 screening questions above 2. Include the phrase "I design for production" 3. Link your portfolio (Behance, Dribbble, personal site, or Google Drive — we don't care where, we care what's in it) 4. Include at least 2 examples of **physical product packaging** you designed (not mockups — actual printed products) 5. Tell us your rate expectation and availability **Applications without portfolio links or screening answers will not be reviewed.** We review applications within 48 hours. Shortlisted candidates will receive the paid test task within one week.

title: UX Designer – eCommerce & Conversion Rate Optimization
job_title: UX Designer – eCommerce & Conversion Rate Optimization
description: We are looking for a UX Designer who truly understands how users behave — and how great design directly drives revenue. This role is NOT about making things look pretty. It's about making things WORK. --- WHO WE ARE We are a performance-driven eCommerce team. Every design decision we make is measured by one question: Does it convert? We believe in data-backed design, clean user flows, and removing every possible barrier between a visitor and a purchase. UX at our company is a growth tool — not a decoration department. --- WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design and optimize UX flows for eCommerce stores (product pages, PDPs, checkout, cart, landing pages) - Identify conversion bottlenecks and propose testable, hypothesis-driven solutions - Create wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity mockups in Figma - Conduct UX audits on existing stores and present actionable improvements - Collaborate closely with our team to implement and A/B test design changes - Stay current with eCommerce UX best practices, CRO frameworks, and buyer psychology --- OUR UX PRINCIPLES (Read carefully — this defines how we work) 1. Function over aesthetics. A beautiful design that doesn't convert is a failed design. Every element must serve a purpose. 2. Less friction, more revenue. We remove every unnecessary click, scroll, and decision from the user's path to purchase. 3. Design for the user, not for yourself. We don't care if something looks clever. We care if it works for real customers. 4. Data is your compass. Gut feeling is a starting point — not a conclusion. We test, measure, and iterate. 5. Clarity beats creativity. If a user has to think twice, we've already lost them. 6. Mobile-first, always. The majority of eCommerce traffic is mobile. If it doesn't work perfectly on mobile, it doesn't ship. 7. Speed matters. Every second of load time costs conversions. Design must consider performance. --- WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Strong experience in UX design for eCommerce (Shopify, WooCommerce, or similar platforms) - Solid understanding of Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) principles and best practices - Proficiency in Figma — you must be able to design and prototype natively in Figma - Ability to think in user journeys, funnels, and behavioral patterns - Knowledge of A/B testing concepts (Hotjar, Google Optimize, VWO, or similar tools is a plus) - Strong eye for UX copy — microcopy, CTAs, and headlines that convert - Ability to work independently, communicate clearly, and meet deadlines --- HOW TO APPLY — IMPORTANT: Applications without a video will NOT be considered. To apply, you must submit a short video (2–5 minutes) in which you: 1. Walk us through at least one Figma UX design you created for an eCommerce context (product page, checkout, landing page, etc.) 2. Explain WHY you made specific design decisions — focus on conversion and user behavior, not aesthetics 3. If you don't have existing eCommerce projects: Pick any real online store, identify a UX/CRO problem on it, and show us how you would redesign or improve it in Figma. We are more interested in how you THINK than what you've already done. Your video should demonstrate: clear thinking, knowledge of eCommerce UX, and a conversion-first mindset. No video = no review. This is non-negotiable. --- We look forward to meeting designers who design with purpose.
